name: ChartQA
description: A large-scale benchmark for question answering about charts with visual and logical reasoning. It covers 9,608 human-written questions and 23,111 questions generated from human-written chart summaries. The benchmark consists of 20,882 charts curated from four different online sources (Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data, OECD) to ensure variety in visual styles and topics. Questions focus on compositional and visual reasoning, including arithmetic and logical operations over chart data.
creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
citeAs: Masry, A., Long, D. X., Tan, J. Q., Joty, S., & Hoque, E. (2022). ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning. arXiv:2203.10244v1 [cs.CL].
rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four different online sources: Statista (statista.com), Pew Research (pewresearch.org), Our World In Data or OWID (ourworldindata.org), and OECD (oecd.org). For the Pew dataset, only chart images were crawled since the underlying data tables are not available. For the other three sources, the underlying data tables, metadata (e.g., title, chart type), SVG files, and associated text descriptions were extracted. Bounding box information of different chart elements was extracted from SVG files to train data extraction models. Human-authored QA pairs were collected using Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT), and additional QA pairs were generated automatically from human-written Statista chart summaries using a fine-tuned T5 model.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For the Pew dataset, the underlying data tables are not available, so only chart images were crawled. Some T5-generated questions were incomplete or not answerable from the chart (e.g., questions requiring knowledge outside of the chart). A heuristic filter was applied to remove such invalid questions, and the test set of the machine-generated dataset was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Charts and associated data were collected from four online sources: Statista (economy, politics, industry topics), Pew Research (social and economic issues, demographic trends, public opinion), Our World In Data (global issues such as economy, finance, society), and OECD (reports and data analysis for policymaking). Human-written chart summaries from Statista were used to generate machine-based QA pairs.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A T5 model was fine-tuned on the SQuAD QA dataset and applied to human-written chart summaries from Statista to automatically generate questions. The process involved two T5 models: one for answer extraction (trained on SQuAD passage-answer pairs) and one for answer-aware question generation (trained on SQuAD passage-answer-question triples). A heuristic filter was applied to remove questions where the answer could not be found in the chart data table. The test set of the machine-generated dataset was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Charts were crawled from four sources. For Statista, Pew, OWID, and OECD, underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and associated text descriptions were extracted where available. Bounding box information of chart elements was extracted from SVG files. For machine-generated QA pairs, a heuristic filter removed questions whose answers could not be found in the chart data table. The test set of machine-generated QA pairs was manually cleaned. Both human-written (ChartQA-H) and machine-generated (ChartQA-M) QA pairs were randomly split into train, validation, and test sets.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT). In each HIT, workers verified two previously asked questions by other workers and also provided two new QA pairs. Workers were asked to focus on two types of questions for each chart image: compositional questions (containing at least two mathematical/logical operations like sum, difference, and average) and visual questions (referring to visual attributes such as color, height, and length of graphical marks). For each chart, workers provided two questions with answers. The same questions were then answered by another annotator. If both workers' answers exactly matched, the answer was considered correct. Otherwise, answers were manually checked to select the final correct answer. Workers were selected with an acceptance rate of 95% and total accomplished HITs of 5000, and further filtered via a pre-test.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The agreement between crowd workers based on exact matches was 61.04%. A manual check on 500 random samples found the agreement to be 78.55% when considering typos and lexical variations (e.g., '3$' vs '3 dollars', '86.33' vs '86.3'). For machine-generated QA pairs, 1,250 QA pairs were manually analyzed and 86.64% were found to be complete, answerable, and correct given the chart. A manual check on 100 questions with difference/ratio operations found 24% noise in the heuristic-based supervision.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 questions per chart (human-authored); each question answered by at least 2 annotators
rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with an acceptance rate of 95% and total accomplished HITs of 5000. Workers were compensated at a rate consistent with the US minimum wage at the time ($7.25 USD per hour), receiving $0.6 USD per task (estimated 3-5 minutes per task). All annotations were anonymized to protect annotator privacy.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: T5 model fine-tuned on SQuAD for answer extraction and question generation; ChartOCR (Luo et al., 2021) extended for structured data table extraction; CRAFT model (Baek et al., 2019) for text recognition in chart elements; Mask R-CNN with Resnet-101 for visual feature extraction
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/vis-nlp/ChartQA. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described in the paper.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive human attributes are collected as part of this dataset. The dataset consists of charts covering topics such as economy, politics, health, society, and demographic trends. Annotator annotations were anonymized.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to advance Chart Question Answering (ChartQA) systems that help users analyze data visualizations. The authors note that models can be abused to mislead the public about chart content and implications. The dataset covers socially relevant topics including politics, economy, health, and society.
rai:dataBiases: Politics is a common topic among all sources, particularly in the Pew dataset where nearly half of charts are about U.S. Politics & Policy (45.4%). Bar charts are the most common chart type across all datasets. The dataset is constructed from four specific online sources which may not represent all possible chart styles or topics. Machine-generated questions may have domain mismatch issues since the T5 model was fine-tuned on SQuAD.
rai:dataLimitations: Current automatic data extraction approaches are modular and combine deep learning and rule-based methods which are error-prone, especially for real-world charts with diverse styles. Performance decreases when gold data tables are not provided. The VisionTaPas model does not support nested arithmetic operations. Evaluation metrics for chart data extraction do not take extracted textual tokens into consideration. The dataset is limited to bar, line, and pie chart types. Some machine-generated questions may be invalid or unanswerable despite filtering.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing of Chart Question Answering (ChartQA) models. The benchmark is intended to evaluate visual and logical reasoning over charts, including compositional questions (arithmetic/logical operations) and visual questions (referring to visual attributes of chart elements). The authors suggest it can serve as a starting point for addressing challenges in visual and logical reasoning over charts.
